Description
Is crypto mining still profitable in 2021? Complete mining guide for beginners from an expert with years of experience. Latest market trends and secrets of mining profitability.
Cryptocurrency mining profitability in 2021.
Hey guys! I can't say my name is Jihan Wu, but I have enough experience in profitable crypto mining. It is not the first year that I have been mining the main cryptocurrency: I did it both on my equipment and using cloud mining; I did it with both bears and bulls; I did it both profitable and unprofitable.
There is a lot of information on the Internet about the technical specifications of equipment, electricity prices, and what Elon Musk eats. Still, no one would answer if mining cryptocurrency is worth it in 2021 or not. So let's fix this.
Is crypto mining still profitable in 2021?
Due to the complexity of the network and the latest halving, many people think that crypto mining profitability is very low. As if it was left in 2017. But in fact, everything is exactly the opposite. If we look at the Coinbase stats on the total amount of block rewards and transaction fees paid to miners, we can see that miners' revenues are now 50% higher than at the 2017 peak. $60 million a month. Sounds good, doesn't it?
But this is the total income that both corporations with large data centers and private miners received. It is impossible to say exactly how the shares are distributed, but experience suggests that companies received more. It can be understood by the factors that determine crypto mining profitability.
General factors of mining profitability
Hash rate
Bitcoin hash rate is the total computing power of all mining devices connected to the network. It increases and forces you to buy more powerful and expensive equipment in order to get a mining reward. But if this is quite feasible for a large company, then not every private miner has the capital to re-equip his rig.
An increase in the hash rate leads to an increase in the difficulty of the network, which means that the profitability per device decreases. Therefore, those who have many of the most powerful devices win.
Network difficulty
Network difficulty is an indicator of how difficult it is to mine a new block for the network. The higher the difficulty, the more computing power is needed to mine the same number of blocks. This process makes the blockchain more resistant to attacks.
The difficulty changes proportionally to the hash rate. This parameter is also common for everyone.
Block reward
The block reward or mining reward is the amount of cryptocurrency that the miner receives for creating a new block (finding a solution that will allow the block to be on the blockchain). Initially, the block reward on the bitcoin network was 50 BTC (sic!). However, this did not last long. The block reward structure in Bitcoin is designed so that reward is halved every 210,000 blocks.
Since the block time of bitcoin (time to create a block) is 10 minutes, there is a decrease in the block reward approximately every four years. At the moment of writing this text the block mining reward is 6.25 BTC. Thanks to halving, bitcoin is not afraid of inflation and this increases the value of each coin.
Individual factors of mining profitability
Electricity cost
But enough about rewards! How about costs and entry thresholds? These are perhaps the main factors that determine your mining income. And in most cases, they are difficult to change. The cost of electricity depends mainly on your location.
If you are lucky and were born in Venezuela, then congratulations! Your electricity is cheap, which means mining cryptocurrency will be worth it. If you live in Germany, then forget about home mining. Or just move to another country...
https://www.statista.com/statistics/263492/electricity-prices-in-selected-countries/
Cost of equipment
It is the most exciting part, especially in 2021. The market faced a shortage of microchips, and the cost of equipment skyrocketed. Yes, along with the cost of bitcoin, the equipment that mines it has risen. If earlier WhatsMiner M31 S 66 TH/s cost $2250, now its price is about $5000. To recoup the cost of this miner, you need about 416 days (with the profit of $12 per day).
But how long will a crypto mining rig be profitable? Look again at the graphs of network difficulty and hash rate. And don't forget about the shortage of equipment! Even if you have money for it and it will be relevant for a long time, it is not a fact that you will find where to buy it. Manufacturers are loaded with orders until the end of 2021.
Solution
By 2021, the market situation has developed so that it is difficult for an ordinary person like me or you to get income by mining bitcoins at home. Large associations of miners and corporations take all profits.
Therefore, I consider cloud mining to be the best option in the current situation (that’s why cryptouniverse.io was created). It allows you to rent the computing power in a large data center and receive personal income. By the way, you don't need any hardware at all! You don't want to heat Siberia, do you?
Conclusion
Throughout the history of Bitcoin, it was possible to earn money by mining it. And today crypto mining is profitable. But there have always been different ways. We have passed the era of CPU mining, GPU mining, and mining on ASICs. Well... welcome to the new era of cloud mining!

Is crypto mining profitable? Crypto Mining X gives you the answer
Is crypto mining profitable?
October 4, 2021 by cryptominingx
Whether crypto mining is worth it or not is one of the big questions in the crypto world.. Currently this can be answered pretty precisely: Yes – crypto mining is profitable for most people.. Or to put it in other words: At this point I cannot mention a place on earth where the variable cost would exceed the crypto mining cash flow.
But you should of course be aware. Many factors can affect the profitability, so what we see next month can be very different from how things look today.
And with that stated, here comes the long answer..
What is crypto mining?
Crypto mining is basically the process of using “computer power” to verify and register transactions on the blockchain – and in return receiving cryptocurrency as a reward for your efforts.
Crypto mining is necessary to keep the ledger on the blockchain up to date – at least for crypto currencies that uses Proof of Work (PoW) for verification.
Examples of crypto currencies that uses Proof of Work are the two biggest crypto currencies: Ethereum (ETH) and Bitcoin (BTC).
The payment for mininers can consist of two different parts: The crypto reward and transaction fees.
The crypto rewards are “extra coins” waiting to be payed to miners. If you have ever heard about “mining reward halving”, this refers to the event of lowering the rewards being payed to miners. In the case of Bitcoin, the halving event occurs approximately every 4 years. This means that the payout, for the same amount of work, is halved. Historically this has though been offset by the increasing crypto prices and increased efficiency of hardware
The transaction fees are paid by crypto owners when buying, selling or transferring cryptocurrencies. These fees are variable depending on the amount of “traffic” on the blockchain. The more traffic, the higher fees. The transaction fees partly end up at the miners.
Which types of crypto mining exist?
The two main types of crypto mining are GPU mining and ASIC mining. Other types of crypto mining exist as well, but mining solutions as CPU mining and FPGA mining are basically not relevant anymore.
Let me give you the short explanation of the difference between GPU- and ASIC-mining, before we jump to the calculations on crypto mining profitability.
GPU mining
This is basically where the miner uses the strong calculation power on GPUs/graphic cards to solve puzzles necessary to verify and register transactions on the blockchain.
Different GPUs have different calculation power, which is also known as the hashrate. The higher hashrate, the faster calculations can be made and the more you will earn as crypto miner.
Currently GPUs can be used to mine cryptocurrencies as Ethereum (ETH), Ravencoin (RVN) and EthereumClassic (ETC).
You can find a list at https://whattomine.com/ that shows which coins can be mined with GPUs. The list also shows which cryptocurrencies are most profitable to mine, but be aware that a lot of factor effect this, so it can change rapidly..  This will be explained in more detail in the “ How do you calculate crypto mining profitability?”-section in this article.
ASIC mining
ASIC miners revolutionised Bitcoin mining when they were introduced. These are machines designed specifically for Bitcoin mining and they are extremely effective for this purpose. Where GPUs can be used for gaming and other activities, ASIC miners only have one purpose in life.
There is currently a high demand for ASIC miners, which cannot be covered by the production of these. So if you would like to get into the business of mining Bitcoin, you should prepare for some waiting time.
How do you calculate crypto mining profitability?
And now to the really interesting part: How do you actually calculate if crypto mining is profitable?
I will show you the equation and take you through the different variables and explain them in greater detail. After giving you the explanations, I will show you a real life calculation example based on our own mining activities.
The following explanations and calculations will be based on Ethereum mining, but the same principles apply to other mining activities as well.
An now for the calculations..
Revenue
You revenue will be based on 3 different overall factors:
Your produced hashrate
The mining network hashrate
The mining network rewards and fees
The crypto currency price
Costs
One-time costs
Variable costs
A real life Ethereum (ETH) profitability calculation
Be aware – profitability can quickly change
Even though crypto mining might be profitable now, different factors can change quickly. Here are what we see as your 5 main risks if you´re a crypto miner:
Crypto price drop
This point is pretty simple. If the price of the crypto currency you mine changes, then your mining profitability will change as well.
If the price of Ethereum goes down by 10%, then your payout in USD will go down by 10% as well (if every other parameter stays the same).
With the huge volatility of cryptocurrencies in mind, you can almost be sure that large decrease in price will happen. The question then is whether these will be short- or longterm decreases.
You will of course also have the upside of potential increases in price.
Crypto network hashrate increase
To put it simple, your share of the total network rewards will be your produced hashrate divided by the total network hashrate. If the network hashrate increases, while your produced hashrate is steady, then your share of rewards will decrease.
Different events can make the network hashrate increase significantly, but technologic development in regards to minehardware will be your enemy, if you no longer invest in new mining equipment yourselves.
Here is a chart that shows the development in network hashrate for Ethereum doing the last 12 months:
As shown, the ETH network hashrate has more than doubled during the last 12 months. For your profitability to stay the same during such a period, the price of ETH needs to increase by the same ration as the network hashrate (if every other variable stay the same).
The network hashrate of Ethereum is expected to keep increasing as long as the coin is significantly profitable to mine.
